_comment: Intel Arc B-series specs from published Intel sources. Each row cites the SKU spec page or Intel datasheet. Compute peaks are not read from per-card totals: the roofline computes each tier as units x ops_per_clk x peak_clock_mhz from arch_rates (see _arch_rates_comment). BF16, FP16 and FP8 matmuls run on the XMX BF16 tier; W4A8 paths run on the XMX INT8 tier (the activation side governs throughput). Die: the G21 or G31 name pci.ids gives each PCI device ID. Core counts and bus widths are Intel's: B580 and B60 are G21 with 20 Xe cores and a 192-bit bus, B50 is G21 with 16 Xe cores and a 128-bit bus at 14 Gbps, B65 is G31 with 20 Xe cores and B70 is G31 with 32, both on a 256-bit bus. B580 FP32: 14.59 is 160 vector engines x 32 FLOP/clk x the 2850 MHz clock at which Intel's published 233 INT8 TOPS is reached. pci_device_id: the value shown in brackets by `xpu-smi discovery` / `lspci -d 8086:` (e.g. `Intel(R) Graphics [0xe223]` is arc-pro-b70). Source: each SKU's Intel spec page (PCI device ID field), matching the pci.ids database names (Battlemage G21 [Arc Pro B50] 0xe212, Battlemage G31 [Arc Pro B65] 0xe222); B580, B60 and B70 also confirmed by lspci on the hardware.
_arch_rates_comment: Per-unit, per-clock throughput for each architecture. A peak is units x ops_per_clk x peak_clock_mhz, so every total in this file can be checked by hand. Intel's spec pages give per-card totals, so these per-unit rates are derived from them: dividing each card's published INT8 TOPS by (XMX engines x peak clock) gives 512, and its published FP32 by (vector engines x peak clock) gives 32. XMX FP16/BF16 is half the INT8 rate, the ratio Intel's oneAPI GPU optimization guide documents for Xe-HPG and Xe-HPC. peak_clock_mhz is the clock that reproduces Intel's published peaks: the Graphics Max Dynamic Clock where Intel lists one (B50, B70), the Graphics Clock for the B60 and B65. The B580 lists only a Graphics Clock; its peak_clock_mhz is 2850, the clock at which Intel's published 233 INT8 TOPS is reached.
_framework_factors_comment: Roofline efficiency knobs. MFU = Model FLOP Utilization (compute roof, prefill). BWE = Bandwidth Efficiency (memory roof, decode). Ranges are community-typical for the named runtime, not measurements from any specific stack. Width reflects 'maturing kernel coverage' as the lower bound and 'well-tuned kernel' as the upper. The skill emits a band, not a point estimate. Use scripts/calibrate.py to anchor these to your specific (image, device) combination; it overrides the band for that run. mfu_by_tier gives a compute tier its own band. The xmx_bf16 bands are a stop-gap: they are the old bands divided by 4, because BF16 prefill used to be modelled on the vector FP16 peak, which is a quarter of the XMX BF16 peak, so they reproduce the BF16 and FP8 predictions made before the change. Replace them with bands from a calibrate.py run once one exists; calibrate.py already measures against the XMX BF16 peak.
_quant_comment: Bytes per parameter and which arch_rates compute tier each quant routes to on Xe2 XMX. W4A8 (awq/gptq/auto-round/inc) uses the INT8 DPAS tier because activations are int8. Plain FP8 weights stay on the XMX BF16 tier: Battlemage XMX has no native FP8 matmul DPAS, so kernels dequantize FP8 to BF16 before the matmul. FP8 still saves memory bytes (1.0 vs 2.0 per weight) but does not get the int8-tier compute speedup.
